name: Saturn from Voyager 1, October 11, 1980
blurb: The ringed planet, about 120,500 kilometers across at the equator. Seen by Voyager 1's narrow-angle camera through orange, green, blue and violet filters: visible light only, 0.40 to 0.62 µm.
story: Saturn filling much of the frame, fully lit, from about 44 million kilometers away, 33 days before Voyager 1's closest approach to Saturn on November 12, 1980. Its rings are billions of chunks of ice and rock, from dust-sized grains to pieces as big as a house.
